programme.title: Nyingchi Ep.1
programme.desc: Join Tianran He in Nyingchi, Xizang Autonomous Region. Fed by the Yarlung Zangbo River and abundant rainfall, this lush subtropical region is home to some of Xizan’g most unique scenery. From sacred mountains and ancient monasteries, to cruising along Nyingchi’s mother river, wandering alpine meadows and savoring stone pot chicken – a beloved local delicacy, Tianran uncovers the beauty of Nyingchi.

programme.title: The Pulse
programme.desc: “The Pulse” features musicians performing amidst Guizhou’s stunning natural scenery, bringing to life a harmonious blend of music and landscape.

programme.title: Jingmai Wanderings: A Symphony of Humans and Tea
programme.desc: As a UNESCO World Heritage site, Mount Jingmai embodies the ecological wisdom of forest–tea symbiosis and the rich cultural diversity of its ethnic communities. It plays a vital role in biodiversity conservation and the preservation of traditional tea culture.\nThis episode follows the stories of representative individuals to explore three key themes — heritage preservation, ecological sustainability, and youth empowerment — revealing the unique charm and sustainable development model of Mount Jingmai.

programme.title: Pingyao Hand-Polished Lacquer Art
programme.desc: Pingyao is an old town with a history of over 2,700 years in the north of China, in Shanxi Province. The rich cultural heritage it built up over the centuries eventually gave rise to a very special art—Tuiguang lacquerware. This hand-polished lacquerware, unique to Pingyao, is recognized as one of the four representative lacquerwares of China.

programme.title: Kung fu journey up Wudang Mountains
programme.desc: Located in central China's Hubei Province, Wudang Mountains is a UNESCO World Natural and Cultural Heritage site recognized as the cradle of Wudang kung fu and as a renowned Taoist sanctuary. Every year, young students from different parts of China flock to these well-established kung fu academies to experience a childhood like no other. Li Weimu and Li Muzi study at two separate kung fu academies, and are following their own paths at Wudang Mountains.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-5 Xingyi Quan
programme.desc: In Episode 5, Kleber travels to Shanxi, the birthplace of Xingyi Quan. He follows Master Cao Bing, a traditional Xingyi Quan teacher and modern combat coach, from Taiyuan’s noodle shops to Pingyao’s ancient streets, and from centuries-old vinegar breweries to Guandi temples, exploring Xingyi Quan’s deep links to Shanxi’s merchant culture and history.\nMaster Cao breaks down the core principles of the “Five Elements and Twelve Forms”, and shows in his modern gym how techniques found in Muay Thai and Jiu-Jitsu can be integrated without losing Xingyi Quan’s philosophical core, guided by the mindset of taking only what is essential. Set against ancient sites such as Yongle Palace, this episode shows how true inner strength is like traditional timber architecture: stable, balanced, and built from within.

programme.title: Foodwise: Haikou
programme.desc: Welcome to Haikou, also known as the Coconut City! Join Tianran He in experiencing the unique culinary culture and urban character of this tropical paradise. From light and sweet coconut chicken hotpot to refreshing herbal desserts and spicy rice soup - a local favourite, every bite tells the story of the city's laid-back charm and beauty. We'll explore everything from Haikou's winding alleys and mangrove forests, to the culture of its southeast Asian diaspora, so come and discover this magical destination with us.

programme.title: Foodwise: Hainan's Four Famous Dishes
programme.desc: The stunning east coast of Hainan in southeast China, attract numerous visitors to travel. The reason that people tend to visit Hianan not only because of the beautiful beach view but also delicious local cuisine in Hainan. Hainan’s four famous dishes is Chicken, duck, goat and crab. In Wenchang, the ancestral home of many overseas Chinese, people could discover the original version of Hainan Chicken Rice and see how local chickens free range on coconut meat. In Qionghai, seat of the Boao Forum for Asia, you may dine on duck and goat, before feasting on crab in the surfer haven of Wanning.

programme.title: Four Faces of Muqam
programme.desc: Muqam is a performing art with its roots in the folklore of Xinjiang. Rather like an encyclopedia, Muqam is a record of the history and lifestyle of the local Uygur people. It originated in folk culture, with lyrics that covered everything from philosophical aphorisms to folk tales. Muqam is a vehicle for Uygur people to express their feelings and ideas. As such, it is an integral part of Xinjiang culture—and even the culture of the Silk Road.\nIn the episode, the host travels around the Kashgar area, learning about the history and art of Muqam.

programme.title: Thrill Seeker’s Guide to China: Mount Siguniang
programme.desc: In this episode, Host Tianran He is on a mission: To reach the summit of Mount Siguniang, a towering snowcapped mountain in southwestern China. Together with his friend Ma Chunlin, a photographer for National Geographic, they trek through one of China’s most beautiful and biodiverse hiking routes, before making for base camp. But with worsening weather conditions and severe altitude sickness, the odds are stacked against them. Ten years ago, Tianran failed his attempt at climbing Mount Siguniang’s First Peak – this time, he’s all in.

programme.title: Foodwise: Xishuangbanna Ep.1
programme.desc: What's not to love about Xishuangbanna? From dazzling night markets to lush bamboo forests, 800-year old tea trees to close encounters with elephants, this tropical city in southwest China has everything, and is where the story of tea begins. Join Foodwise for all the Pu'er tea you can drink and feast on everything from banana flowers to \"elephant food\".

programme.title: Foodwise: Xishuangbanna Ep.2
programme.desc: Come get soaked at the Dai people's New Year celebrations! We'll check out buzzing street markets packed with barbecued meats and spicy fruits, crash a foodie auction, and even take part in a rowdy competition, catching fish with our bare hands in the river. All this before hiking through an actual rainforest. We're going to need all the good tea and food we can get.

programme.title: The Sichuan Zhuqin
programme.desc: Sichuan Zhuqin is a national intangible cultural heritage in China. Nowadays, its performances are constantly innovated, with new styles such as ensemble emerging. Creators have broken traditional performance methods, integrating Zhuqin with traditional Chinese instruments like the guzheng and erhu, and also experimenting with contemporary music forms such as rap and folk rock, aiming to make this traditional art appeal to more young audiences.

programme.title: Breathing new life into century-old Yueju Opera
programme.desc: Yueju Opera is one of the five major Chinese operas. It is skillful in narration and sentiment and is popular across China. This timeless form of intangible cultural heritage now has new apprentices. We followed a young duo of Yueju Opera performers: eleven-year-old Wang Yuhan and her stage partner, nine-year-old Huang Xinru in Ningbo, Zhejiang Province, as they shared kindred spirits in inheriting the performing art of Yueju Opera.

programme.title: Thrill Seeker’s Guide to China: Changbai Mountain
programme.desc: An unforgettable adventure awaits amidst the breathtaking landscapes of Changbai Mountain! Embark on a trek through pristine birch forests, marvel at the majestic power of the world's deepest volcanic waterfall, and uncover hidden gems along the way. Indulge in soaking in natural hot springs and experience exhilarating rafting down mountain streams, all leading to the final destination: Tianchi Lake, a heavenly oasis nestled in the clouds. Join the Travelogue team as we delve into the beauty of Changbai Mountain.

programme.title: Nyingchi Ep.2
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He continues his journey through Nyingchi, Xizang Autonomous Region. He meets the Lhoba people, China’s smallest ethnic group, who show him their traditional hunting attire. At a sacred lake, Tianran visits an ancient monastery and witnesses the 3000-year-old dance of the Gongbo Tibetans, before venturing to a remote village to experience their their way of life.

programme.title: Back to the Land: Exploring new life in rural China
programme.desc: When we think of the countryside, what colour comes to mind? From dazzling night markets to lush bamboo forests, 800-year old tea trees to close encounters with elephants, this tropical city in southwest China has everything, and is where the story of tea begins. Join Foodwise for all the Pu'er tea you can drink and feast on everything from banana flowers to \"elephant food\".

programme.title: Foodwise: Xishuangbanna Ep.2
programme.desc: Come get soaked at the Dai people's New Year celebrations! We'll check out buzzing street markets packed with barbecued meats and spicy fruits, crash a foodie auction, and even take part in a rowdy competition, catching fish with our bare hands in the river. All this before hiking through an actual rainforest. We're going to need all the good tea and food we can get.

programme.title: The Sichuan Zhuqin
programme.desc: Sichuan Zhuqin is a national intangible cultural heritage in China. Nowadays, its performances are constantly innovated, with new styles such as ensemble emerging. Creators have broken traditional performance methods, integrating Zhuqin with traditional Chinese instruments like the guzheng and erhu, and also experimenting with contemporary music forms such as rap and folk rock, aiming to make this traditional art appeal to more young audiences.

programme.title: Breathing new life into century-old Yueju Opera
programme.desc: Yueju Opera is one of the five major Chinese operas. It is skillful in narration and sentiment and is popular across China. This timeless form of intangible cultural heritage now has new apprentices. We followed a young duo of Yueju Opera performers: eleven-year-old Wang Yuhan and her stage partner, nine-year-old Huang Xinru in Ningbo, Zhejiang Province, as they shared kindred spirits in inheriting the performing art of Yueju Opera.

programme.title: Thrill Seeker’s Guide to China: Changbai Mountain
programme.desc: An unforgettable adventure awaits amidst the breathtaking landscapes of Changbai Mountain! Embark on a trek through pristine birch forests, marvel at the majestic power of the world's deepest volcanic waterfall, and uncover hidden gems along the way. Indulge in soaking in natural hot springs and experience exhilarating rafting down mountain streams, all leading to the final destination: Tianchi Lake, a heavenly oasis nestled in the clouds. Join the Travelogue team as we delve into the beauty of Changbai Mountain.

programme.title: Nyingchi Ep.2
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He continues his journey through Nyingchi, Xizang Autonomous Region. He meets the Lhoba people, China’s smallest ethnic group, who show him their traditional hunting attire. At a sacred lake, Tianran visits an ancient monastery and witnesses the 3000-year-old dance of the Gongbo Tibetans, before venturing to a remote village to experience their their way of life.

programme.title: The Pulse
programme.desc: “The Pulse” features musicians performing amidst Guizhou’s stunning natural scenery, bringing to life a harmonious blend of music and landscape.

programme.title: Back to the Land: Exploring new life in rural China
programme.desc: When we think of the countryside, what colour comes to mind? The answer lies in Wuxin—Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal and Water—an ancient rhythm that still pulses beneath China’s landscapes.\nIn this programme, we explore how the colours of Wuxing come to life through the traditions of China’s ethnic minority groups. From Lugu Lake’s matrilineal water world and the metal-hued fire of the Yi Torch Festival, to Dali’s earth-driven crafts, Guizhou’s wooden Dong dwellings, and the volcanic winds of Inner Mongolia’s new nomadic life—the Five Elements guide the stories of people reconnecting with land, culture and community.

programme.title: A Journey on Water from Wuxi to Yixing
programme.desc: Water has always been the heartbeat of human civilization, nurturing the cities it weaves through. In eastern China, the Grand Canal flows across Wuxi, etching its path through history. From the first drops that carved out its waterways to the thriving metropolis we see today, Wuxi’s story is inseparable from the canal that gave it life. In this episode, we uncover how the waters have shaped Wuxi’s identity. This is the story of a city born of water, where the past and present flow together, crafting the future.

This timeless form of intangible cultural heritage now has new apprentices. programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Wing Chun
programme.desc: Martial arts lover Kleber Battaglia is on a mission: To seek out China's kungfu masters, and learn their secrets. From explosive Wing Chun to fluid Taiji Quan, slippery Snake Style to elegant White Crane, he'll learn hidden moves and ancient techniques for defeating powerful opponents. But ?there’s more to kungfu than combat: From culture and philosophy, to wellness and insights from the natural world, Kleber will discover that contained within every kick, strike and throw, is the condensed wisdom of the ancient masters. This is Kungfu-wise.\nKleber travels to Foshan, the birthplace of Wing Chun. A practitioner of this style, he seeks out masters of two different lineages: Ip Man and Snake Style. First he visits the Ip Man lineage, based on the legendary kungfu master whose life story spawned hundreds of martial arts movies, with Bruce Lee counting among his students. With Ip Man Wing Chun, Kleber learns how to create powerful short strikes perfectly suited to fighting in Foshan’s narrow alleys. With Snake Style, he experiences unique training methods that give its practitioners superhuman flexibility, allowing them to stick to their opponents, and even fight on boats in canals.

programme.title: Foodwise: Huangshan Ep.1
programme.desc: Tianran and Hannah climb Mount.Huangshan, one of China's most famous mountains, sampling its delicate green tea and the rich flavors of Anhui cuisine, and explore the region's ancient villages and lush bamboo forests featured in the blockbuster film \"Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon\".

programme.title: Foodwise: Huangshan Ep.2
programme.desc: In Huangshan, Anhui Province, the hosts enjoy a cup of Queen Elizabeth II's favorite tea, as well as the oldest green tea to be exported Europe, and get hands on with quirky local delicacies ranging from \"word candy\" and tofu made of leaves, to the downright funky flavors of hairy tofu and stinky mandarin fish.

programme.title: The Tongliang Dragon Dance
programme.desc: The Tongliang Dragon Dance is a traditional performance art rooted in Chongqing’s Tongliang District, characterized by its elaborate dragon props and dynamic choreography. Originating in the Ming Dynasty and flourishing during the Qing, this vibrant folk tradition has regained its brilliance in modern times and earned international acclaim. The dance consists of two main branches: the dragon lantern dance—featuring forms like the Grand Wriggling Dragon, the Fire Dragon, and the Straw Dragon—and the festive lantern dance, which includes acts such as “Carp Leaps Over the Dragon Gate,” “Mudfish Eating Dumplings,” and “Three Dragons.” Steeped in cultural symbolism, the Tongliang Dragon Dance expresses values of unity, vitality, and harmony with nature. While a few iconic forms like the Fire Dragon remain widely recognized, many others are on the verge of extinction and in urgent need of preservation. In this episode, the host travels to Chongqing to meet with four inheritors of the Tongliang Dragon Dance. Through their stories, we uncover the rich legacy of this dazzling tradition, explore the deep roots of dragon culture in the region, and trace the origins of one of China’s most awe-inspiring folk arts.

programme.title: Painting beyond the spectrum
programme.desc: In many ways, 12-year-old Zhu Jingxiu is just like any other boy his age. He is skilled in drawing, enjoys playing the piano, loves to ride his bicycle, and likes to use his mobile phone to film videos of traffic and skyscrapers.

programme.title: Wenzhou
programme.desc: Tianran He is in Wenzhou, southeast China — a city famed for its self-made millionaires. Here he meets the first Chinese shoemaker to expand overseas, and hears the stories of other local entrepreneurs. Along the way, he samples traditional snacks, visits some of China’s oldest lighthouses, and enjoys an evening of Ou Opera. He also learns the craft of papermaking, before heading into the hills to soak in hot springs and wander across ancient covered bridges.
